courses.title: Intro.Labour Studies
courses.description: Introduces key concepts and approaches for understanding the character and organization of work, employment relations, worker’s rights, and labour movements in contemporary society. Explores who does paid and unpaid work and under what conditions through the study of trends and issues, including migration and immigration, unionization, precarious employment, and automation.

courses.title: Labour Research for Social Chg
courses.description: Introduces students to labour research through methodology and research methods for social change. Explores what methodology is, the methods common in labour and community-based research, and understandings of social justice. Students gain experience of quantitative and qualitative approaches through hands-on learning, including survey research, interviews, and ethnography. Focuses on using and interpreting a range of data for social justice and social change projects.

courses.title: Labour, Social Media, and News
courses.prerequisiteText: LBST 100 or LBST 101 or on permission of instructor.
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of the contemporary structure, issues, and perceptions of labour unions and other forms of working-class organization and social movements. The treatment of labour in the media and popular culture will provide an understanding of how labour is viewed in society, how labour views itself, and how working-class culture informs and is informed by the larger culture.

courses.title: Gendering Economy
courses.prerequisiteText: 30 units including LBST 100 or three units in GSWS or WS or GDST.
courses.description: Takes a broad approach to gender, placing it dialogue with race and ethnicity, class, nation, and space, to think through the complex dynamic between gender and labour from a variety of perspectives. Explores workers’ lived experiences of gender regimes while critically examining how gender ‘matters’ within the workplace.

courses.title: Crit Pol Econ of Labour Market
courses.description: An exploration of critical and radical political economy traditions in Labour Studies with a focus on how these approaches have diverged from, and provided alternatives to, classical and orthodox economic understandings of labour and labour markets.

courses.title: Unfree Labour and Modern Slave
courses.description: An exploration of the expanding forms of unfree labour in capitalist economies as products of changing labour processes, global labour markets, and the policies of neoliberalism and 'austerity'.

courses.title: Migration, Migrants, and Work
courses.description: Global labour migration has increased substantially in the last several decades. What factors contribute to the current wave of labour migration? Which countries send and receive migrants, and what is the role of internal migration? What challenges do migrant workers face in their host countries? This course will examine these questions to uncover the nature, trends and impacts of this growing phenomenon.

courses.title: Canadian Labour Law
courses.description: An introduction to labour and employment law in Canada, covering both union and non-union sectors. The course will focus variously on: the principles and practice of the BC Labour Relations Code, the Canada Labour Code, BC Employment Standards Act. BC Human Rights Code, the Workers Compensation Act (WorkSafeBC), and the contested history of labour legislation and related common law.
